title: Open: The Philosophy and Practices that are Revolutionizing Education and Science
abstract: Affordable education. Transparent science. Accessible scholarship. These ideals are slowly becoming a reality thanks to the open education, open science, and open access movements. Running separate—if parallel—courses, they all share a philosophy of equity, progress, and justice. This book shares the stories, motives, insights, and practical tips from global leaders in the open movement.

narrative:
Short impact summary

Open: The Philosophy and Practices that are Revolutionizing Education and Science has clear scholarly traction and active use. It has 103 citations, placing it in the top 10% most-cited works for its field and year, alongside 14,287 downloads that suggest sustained reader demand. The book also appears in teaching-related contexts, has a formal review, and is aligned with Quality Education.

Full narrative

Published by Ubiquity Press in 2017, Open has become a reference point for work on open education, open science, and open access. Its citation record shows steady uptake across the years, with especially strong use in the early 2020s and continued citation into 2025 and 2026. The citing literature is concentrated in education and related digital-learning fields, which fits the book’s framing as both a philosophy and a practical guide for open scholarship.

The book’s influence is not limited to citation counts. Usage metrics show substantial engagement, with activity recorded across Google Books, OAPEN, and Ubiquity Press access logs. That pattern indicates that the book is being read and consulted, not only cited. The record also includes two YouTube videos that explicitly link to the book in their metadata or descriptions, suggesting that it is being used in pedagogical and professional development settings.

Community and online discussion are present as well, though modestly, with mentions on Hypothesis and Bluesky. A formal book review is also recorded, adding another layer of external evaluation beyond author or publisher channels. Taken together, these signals show a work that has moved beyond initial publication into ongoing use, discussion, and critique.

The thematic profile of the citing literature underscores the book’s cross-cutting relevance: open education and e-learning dominate, but the surrounding landscape also includes knowledge management, online learning analytics, research data management, and digital technologies in education. This breadth suggests that Open functions as a synthesis text for scholars and practitioners working at the intersection of educational practice, scientific communication, and openness as a policy and ethical framework.

The evidence base is strongest for scholarly and educational uptake, with additional support from library holdings and open-access availability. Public event coverage was not available in the record, so the narrative here rests on citations, usage, teaching adoption, review activity, and the book’s placement within the broader open education literature.
